answer: Preference for one people or faith is common. Pew counted 43 countries with an official religion and 40 more that favour one, including Denmark and the United Kingdom; Greece's constitution names Orthodoxy the prevailing religion. Germany, Greece, Ireland and Armenia give citizenship by descent or ethnic tie; Israel's Law of Return does so for Jews and their relatives, and the Palestinian Basic Law names Islam the official religion. Israel's Declaration of Independence promises complete equality; the 2018 Nation-State law says self-determination is unique to the Jewish people and does not mention equality. Scholars call Israel an ethnic democracy, an ethnocracy or a democracy, and many stress that it also rules millions of non-citizens in the West Bank. The United States limited naturalisation to free white persons in 1790, set national-origins quotas in 1924, and ended them in 1965.

facts.text: Preferring one religion is common: Pew counted 43 of 199 countries with an official state religion and 40 more that favour one, over 80 in all; a survey of 177 countries in 2008 found 41 with a state religion and 77 that clearly favoured certain religions.

sources.title: Many Countries Favor Specific Religions, Officially or Unofficially
sources.quote: More than 80 countries favor a specific religion, either as an official, government-endorsed religion or by affording one religion preferential treatment over other faiths

sources.publisher: Springer (State and Religion: An Economic Approach)
sources.title: State and Religion: An Economic Approach
sources.quote: 77 countries (44%) clearly favored certain religions; and 41 countries (23%) endorsed one or more religions as the official state religion.

sources.title: A World Survey of Religion and the State
sources.quote: only a minority of states, including a minority of democracies, have separation of religion and state

facts.text: Denmark's constitution makes the Evangelical Lutheran Church the established church, supported by the state; Pew lists Denmark and the United Kingdom among 13 states with Christianity as the official religion, nine of them in Europe.

sources.title: Many Countries Favor Specific Religions, Officially or Unofficially
sources.quote: Nine of these countries are in Europe, including the United Kingdom, Denmark, Monaco and Iceland.

sources.title: Religious Rights - Denmark
sources.quote: The Evangelical Lutheran Church shall be the Established Church of Denmark, and, as such, it shall be supported by the State.

facts.text: The Church of England is the legally established church in England, with the monarch as supreme governor and automatic seats for some senior bishops in the House of Lords; Pew counts the United Kingdom among states with a Christian official religion.

sources.title: Factsheet: The Church of England
sources.quote: the Church of England remains the legally established church, with the monarch as its supreme governor and the automatic right for some of its most senior bishops to have seats in the House of Lords.

sources.title: Church and State in the UK (Constitution Unit paper)

contested.text: How to classify Israel. Sammy Smooha: an 'ethnic democracy'. Oren Yiftachel: an 'ethnocracy' with a democratic facade. The Times of Israel and New York Times pages on the Nation-State Law, the Greek Parliament and Library of Congress pages, the Wiley page of Smooha (2002), Yiftachel's own paper and Britannica's Church of England page blocked the checker; each was replaced by a readable page or removed.

not_claimed: That preferring one people or religion is harmless: it can disadvantage minorities, and several of these states have been criticised for it.
That other countries' practices make any specific Israeli law just, or any other country's law just.
That Israel is, or is not, a democracy in every respect; the card gives indices and the scholarly disagreement.
That the United States has never been, or is now, closed to immigration; it states what the laws said when.
